dataset.source: UCI Machine Learning Repository – Bike Sharing Dataset

models.name: Naive (same-hour last week)
models.notes: All 4376 test rows have a valid 168-hour lag (references train set)

models.name: Ridge Regression
models.notes: Ridge performs worse than naive; demand is highly non-linear and Ridge cannot capture the bimodal daily pattern

models.name: GradientBoosting (Main)
models.notes: LightGBM fallback used due to Windows/Python3.12 access violation. HistGBM achieves similar performance.

validation_warnings: Ridge Regression performs WORSE than the naive baseline (MAE 109.9 vs 74.04). This is expected — Ridge cannot capture the bimodal non-linear daily demand pattern. It serves as an illustration, not a competitive baseline.
LightGBM could not be used on Python 3.12 + Windows (access violation in lgb C library). HistGradientBoostingRegressor was used instead. Results are comparable.
SHAP model-agnostic explainer was used (not TreeExplainer) due to HistGBM compatibility. Feature importance values reflect permutation-based attribution, not exact SHAP Shapley values.
The dataset is city-wide aggregate demand, not station-level. Operational recommendations are directional only.
